findings_to_judge.finding: The Army's $117,306,232 firm-fixed-price order for 82 P550 UAS carries a DoD-stated estimated completion date of 2026-07-23 -- nine days inside AeroVironment's fiscal Q1 FY27, which ended 2026-08-01 -- yet consensus has Q1 product-sales revenue at $306.4M, DOWN 2.3% year over year, a number that cannot easily absorb a ~$117M program that did not exist in the year-ago quarter.

The -26.7% twenty-day drawdown is a documented sector-wide positioning unwind with explicitly no company news, layered on a mechanical share overhang: on 2026-08-24 AVAV fell 5% while RCAT -7%, ONDS -5%, UMAC -9% and KTOS -6%, with the report stating 'No company announcement, contract award, earnings release, regulatory action, or analyst rating change has been reported'; separately, 17,425,849 AVAV shares were issued to the BlueHalo seller and Arlington Capital sponsors, of which 40% (about 6.97M shares, roughly 5.6 days of the 1.25M-share ADV) came off lock-up on 2026-05-01 with a further 30% due 2026-11-01.

The largest good news in this company's history is already spent and none of it is in tonight's numbers: the $464.8M E-HEL award (2026-09-02) is an Other Transaction Agreement ceiling for deliveries 'well into the dozens' spread over 'the next few years' -- a January Army draft solicitation sought up to 24 systems over five years -- it was awarded 32 days after the reported quarter ended, and AVAV gave back the entire intraday +6% pop it produced within four sessions and then failed to respond at all to the first international LOCUST order (>$50M, 2026-09-08).
